topic: 最弱项目补强与迁移复测 · Independent new scenario: competing accounts of social and technical change
grammarFocus: 针对个人错误选择练习；每次订正后用新题检查，而不只重做旧题。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.
sourcePolicy: Project-original scenario; simulated figures and people; no copied official test, textbook, GitHub PDF or third-party audio.
title: The Repair Shop on Maple Street
instructions: 阅读下面的文章，回答10个问题。文章和题目均为模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思试题，也不代表任何分数。先通读全文，再做题。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。
passage:
A
When the Maple Street Repair Shop opened in 2019, it had one workbench, two volunteers, and a simple rule: fix first, replace last. The shop occupies a former garage in the centre of town. People bring in broken lamps, torn coats, and old radios, and volunteers try to repair them free of charge. If a repair is impossible, the item is sent to a recycling centre rather than thrown away. The shop's growth has been striking. In its first year, it repaired 312 items; by 2023, that figure had reached 1,140. Over the same period, the number of volunteers rose from two to nineteen, most of them retired engineers or hobbyists. The shop does not sell new products. It only repairs what people already own, which keeps costs low and waste lower still. This focus on repair rather than replacement is central to its environmental aims.

B
Maya Chen, the shop's coordinator, says the growth was never planned. 'We expected maybe fifty repairs a year,' she says. 'Then a local newspaper wrote about us. After that, people came from three towns.' The shop now runs a waiting list, and on busy Saturdays the queue reaches the street. Maya adds: 'We never advertise. People find us by word of mouth.' The shop receives no government money. It survives on small donations and on sales of repaired items that owners never collect. In 2022, those sales raised £2,400; in 2023, they raised £3,100. This independence is central to the shop's identity, though it also limits what the volunteers can do, as they must constantly seek small contributions.

C
Not everyone agrees that the shop is a success. Tomasz Nowak, who runs a small electronics shop nearby, argues that free repairs undercut his business. 'People bring me a radio and ask why I charge £30 when Maple Street charges nothing,' he says. 'They don't see that my staff are paid.' Nowak says his repair income fell by about 15 per cent after the Maple Street shop expanded. He does not want the shop to close; he wants it to charge a small fee. Maya rejects this idea. 'If we charge, the poorest people stop coming,' she says. 'And they are exactly the people we want to help.' The disagreement reflects a wider tension between volunteer goodwill and paid local trade, highlighting differing views on fairness and sustainability.

D
A second disagreement concerns skills. The shop's volunteers teach repair classes on Thursday evenings. The classes are free, and they are popular: 140 people attended in 2023. Maya believes the classes spread practical skills across the town. 'Once you fix a lamp, you look at broken things differently,' she says. But a local college lecturer, Dr Helen Osei, is less sure. 'Short classes can create confidence without competence,' she says. 'A two-hour class does not make someone an electrician. Some students may attempt unsafe repairs at home.' Osei would like the shop to offer a longer, certified course. Maya says the shop has no money for certification. She also notes that the shop has recorded no accidents in its five years of classes, a record she treats as evidence that the teaching is sound. This safety record, she argues, shows that volunteers teach responsibly.

E
A third question is environmental. The shop's supporters say repair reduces waste. In 2023, the shop estimates it diverted 4.2 tonnes of goods from landfill. That figure is an estimate, not a measurement, because the shop weighs items only when volunteers remember to do so. A university student, Priya Raman, studied the shop for a class project. She found that 60 per cent of repaired items were still in use six months later; the other 40 per cent had broken again or been thrown away. Raman says the shop should track repairs more carefully. 'The idea is good,' she says. 'The data is weak.' Better records, she argues, would help the shop prove its value to funders and critics alike, and would strengthen its environmental claims.

F
Despite these disagreements, the shop is expanding. In 2024, it plans to open a second branch in the east of the town. The new branch will have four workbenches and a small classroom. Maya wants to hire one paid manager, saying volunteers cannot run two sites alone. Nowak calls the expansion 'a warning sign'. Osei calls it 'an opportunity, if the teaching improves'. Raman calls it 'a test'. The shop's future, it seems, depends on which of these views the town accepts. Each critic raises valid points about money, skills, and evidence, and the expansion will likely intensify these debates.

G
For now, the Maple Street Repair Shop continues its work. On a wet Tuesday in March, a woman brought in a 1970s record player. Two volunteers spent three hours on it, and the player worked again by closing time. The woman paid nothing. She left a box of biscuits for the volunteers. Maya put the biscuits in the staff room and wrote the repair in the shop's notebook. It was repair number 4,006. Such small moments illustrate the shop's daily impact, even as larger questions about its role remain unresolved.

questions.prompt: How many items did the shop repair in its first year?
questions.explanation: 原文A段明确说 'In its first year, it repaired 312 items.' 1,140是2023年的数字，4,006是全文最后的总数。
questions.evidence: In its first year, it repaired 312 items

questions.prompt: What does Maya say about advertising?
options: The shop advertises in a local newspaper.
The shop advertises on the radio.
questions.explanation: B段Maya的原话是 'We never advertise. People find us by word of mouth.' 报纸报道是别人写的，不是商店做的广告。
questions.evidence: We never advertise. People find us by word of mouth.

questions.prompt: Tomasz Nowak wants the Maple Street shop to
questions.explanation: C段说 'He does not want the shop to close. He wants it to charge a small fee.' 所以A错，B对。C段没有提到他希望停课。
questions.evidence: He does not want the shop to close; he wants it to charge a small fee.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: Dr Osei says short classes can create confidence without ______.
questions.explanation: D段Osei的原话是 'Short classes can create confidence without competence.' 空格处应填 competence。
questions.evidence: Short classes can create confidence without competence

questions.prompt: What did Priya Raman find about repaired items?
options: All repaired items were still in use after six months.
60 per cent were still in use six months later.
The shop measured every item carefully.
answers: 60 per cent were still in use six months later.
questions.explanation: E段说 'She found that 60 per cent of repaired items were still in use six months later.' A说全部，错误；C与原文 'The shop weighs items only when volunteers remember to do so.' 矛盾。
questions.evidence: She found that 60 per cent of repaired items were still in use six months later; the other 40 per cent had broken again or been thrown away.

questions.prompt: Which heading best describes paragraph C?
options: A disagreement about money and local business
The history of the shop's building
answers: A disagreement about money and local business
questions.explanation: C段主要讲Nowak认为免费修理影响他的生意，以及Maya拒绝收费，属于关于钱和本地生意的分歧。B段才是建筑历史，D段讲培训。
questions.evidence: Tomasz Nowak, who runs a small electronics shop nearby, argues that free repairs undercut his business.

questions.prompt: True, False or Not Given: The shop has recorded several accidents in its classes.
questions.explanation: D段明确说 'She also notes that the shop has recorded no accidents in its five years of classes.' 与题目相反，所以是False。
questions.evidence: She also notes that the shop has recorded no accidents in its five years of classes

questions.prompt: True, False or Not Given: The 4.2 tonnes figure is based on careful measurement of every item.
questions.explanation: E段说 'That figure is an estimate, not a measurement. The shop weighs items only when volunteers remember to do so.' 所以不是仔细测量，答案为False。
questions.evidence: That figure is an estimate, not a measurement, because the shop weighs items only when volunteers remember to do so.

questions.prompt: True, False or Not Given: The second branch will open in the north of the town.
questions.explanation: F段说 'In 2024, it plans to open a second branch in the east of the town.' 方向是east不是north，所以False。
questions.evidence: In 2024, it plans to open a second branch in the east of the town.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: The woman left a box of ______ for the volunteers.
questions.explanation: G段说 'She left a box of biscuits for the volunteers.' 空格处填 biscuits。
questions.evidence: She left a box of biscuits for the volunteers.

grammar.title: 针对个人错误选择练习：用新题检查，而不是重做旧题
grammar.explanation: 很多同学订正时只是把错题重做一遍，记住的是那道题的答案，而不是规则。正确做法是：先弄清自己错在哪一条规则，然后立刻用全新的句子检查同一规则。本课重点练三条规则：(1) 现在完成时 have/has + 过去分词，表示到现在为止的经历或结果；(2) 被动语态 be + 过去分词，强调动作本身；(3) 比较级 more/less + 形容词，以及 not as ... as 结构。注意：订正后必须换新句子，不要只重做原题。
grammar.example: In 2023, the shop estimates it diverted 4.2 tonnes of goods from landfill.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: The volunteers ______ over 4,000 items since 2019.
questions.explanation: since 2019 表示从过去到现在，用现在完成时 have + 过去分词。repaired 是一般过去时，不能与 since 连用。
questions.evidence: In its first year, the shop repaired 312 items.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: The old radio ______ by two volunteers last Tuesday.
questions.explanation: radio 是动作的承受者，last Tuesday 是过去时间，用一般过去时的被动语态 was + 过去分词。
questions.evidence: Two volunteers spent three hours on it.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: This year's classes are ______ than last year's.
questions.explanation: than 前面用比较级。popular 是多音节形容词，比较级用 more popular。
questions.evidence: The classes are free, and they are popular: 140 people attended in 2023.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: The new branch is not as ______ as the old one.
questions.explanation: not as ... as 中间用形容词原级，不用比较级或最高级。
questions.evidence: The new branch will have four workbenches and a small classroom.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: A certified course ______ by the college next year.
questions.explanation: course 是动作的承受者，next year 表示将来，用 will be + 过去分词构成将来被动。
questions.evidence: Osei would like the shop to offer a longer, certified course.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: Repair income has ______ by about 15 per cent.
questions.explanation: has 后面必须用过去分词，构成现在完成时。fell 是过去式，falling 是现在分词。
questions.evidence: Nowak says his repair income fell by about 15 per cent after the Maple Street shop expanded.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: The shop tracks repairs ______ carefully than Raman would like.
questions.explanation: than 前面需要比较级。carefully 是副词，比较级用 less carefully 表示“不如……仔细”。
questions.evidence: Raman says the shop should track repairs more carefully.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: No accidents ______ recorded in the classes so far.
questions.explanation: accidents 是复数，so far 表示到现在为止，用现在完成时的被动 have been + 过去分词。
questions.evidence: She also notes that the shop has recorded no accidents in its five years of classes.
